title: Joe Rogan renews multimillion-dollar podcast deal with Spotify
detail:
Joe Rogan renews multimillion-dollar podcast deal with Spotify
Joe Rogan stands in the octagon at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles after the light heavyweight bout between Alonzo Menifield of the United States and Iwo Baraniewski of Poland on Sept. 19. (Luke Hales / Getty Images)
Wendy Lee
Thu, October 8, 2026 at 9:37 AM PDT 2 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Spotify on Thursday said it had renewed its deal with Joe Rogan, who leads the audio company's most popular podcast, "The Joe Rogan Experience."

The podcast, which has 18 million followers on Spotify, has been the company's top podcast since 2020. The terms of the multiyear licensing deal were not disclosed. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, reported the deal had an estimated earnout of $250 million.

"The partnership with Spotify has been an amazing fit, and they're incredible to work with," Rogan said in a statement. "I'm extremely happy and excited to continue with them for years to come."

Rogan first entered into an exclusive multiyear podcast deal with Spotify in 2020 in a deal said to be worth $100 million. The partnership was key to driving podcast audiences to Spotify, which at the time was mostly known as a streaming music service.

Read more: Spotify digs in on podcasts with new Hollywood studios

In 2024, the company extended its partnership for "The Joe Rogan Experience" to be distributed on other platforms, and that will continue in the latest deal. Rogan's show was ranked as the top podcast last year on Spotify, YouTube and Apple Podcasts.

"Joe has built something incredibly enduring, and his show continues to resonate with a massive global audience because there's simply nothing else like it," said Jordan Newman, head of content partnerships at Spotify, in a statement.

"The Joe Rogan Experience" has run into controversy, spurring a Spotify boycott in 2022 led by Neil Young over concerns that Rogan and his guests were spreading misinformation related to COVID-19 vaccines. Rogan also received criticism over his use of the N-word on past episodes of his show, for which he later apologized.

Read more: Joe Rogan apologizes for discussing doctored tweet on Spotify podcast

After the backlash, Spotify posted its content moderation rules and said it would add content advisory labels on COVID-related podcasts. Rogan also said he would do a better job of balancing different perspectives.

Young later returned to Spotify in 2024.

Revisions to Earnings Estimates

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

title: Spotify down: App not working in huge outage
detail:
Spotify down: App not working in huge outage
Andrew Griffin
September 29, 2026 1 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Spotify has gone down in a major outage.

Users reported problems listening to music, instead seeing an error messaging indicating that "something went wrong".

But the problem appears to be limited to only some users, and some parts of the app. Some found that playing music seemed to work, for instance, but searching for other songs or artists showed nothing or an error message.

Others found that the errors only appeared to occur on the mobile version of the app, while it loaded as normal on the desktop. Users may therefore be able to work around the problems by trying different parts of the app, or using it on a different device.

The problems began just before 3pm UK time, or 10am in New York, according to tracking website Down Detector.

"We're aware of some issues right now and are checking them out!" the company said on its official page on X, formerly Twitter. It did not give any information about the problem, or when it might be fixed.

Unlike many other large tech platforms, the company does not operate an official status page on its own website.

Spotify says that it has around 800 million users, with 300 million of them paying for a monthly subscription. It is available in 184 different countries.
